answer: Refund-cliff bonds: every identity locks a deposit that refunds fully only after thirty honest epochs; but when many identities share one funding source, the refund rate collapses - the schedule splits like basalt columns that hold one climber yet fracture under a crowd. The fable of cheap scale ends when the thousandth fake's deposit never comes home, and the honest agent drifting through the nebula of identities gets every coin back. Cloning keys turns locked capital into permanent cost, because refunds are paid per funder, not per key.
